newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance volume up on buyout rumor.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance volume up on buyout rumor.

text.p: Trading in shares of Mercury Finance Co spiked up Monday and Tuesday on rumors that the beleaguered sub-prime auto lender may be acquired.

"There's talk that they could possibly be acquired. Personally, I don't put very high probability in it because they don't have audited financials," said Gruntal & Co industry analyst Katrina Blecher.
In early afternoon, more than one million shares in the Northbrook, Ill.-based firm had changed hands, including 726,100 shares in block trades. The shares' value remained unchanged at 2-3/8.
On Monday, more than three million shares changed hands, including a 484,000-share block trade.

Daily trading volume had last crossed the three-million share mark since April 23, when Mercury said it estimated on a preliminary basis that it would lose $48 million to $55 million in the year ended December 31, 1996.

Also on April 23, Arthur Andersen said a review of Mercury's books continued and the firm would render an opinion by the end of May. Mercury said it expected the opinion would raise doubts about its ability to continue as a going concern.
One analyst called trading in the past two days "foolish speculation."
Another said, "There are some people out there who are willing to take a little flier on a rumor and figure they're capped on the downside."
